question.problem:
The weights of sugar in different types of cookies are normally distributed with a mean of $15\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{g}.$ Suppose $16$ cookies are selected randomly. What is the probability that the mean amount of sugar per cookie for this sample will be more than $14.7\,\text{g},$ but less than $15.3\,\text{g}?$ *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2420\,$ $\,0.2389\,$ $\,0.2358\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2743\,$ $\,0.2709\,$ $\,0.2676\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.3085\,$ $\,0.3050\,$ $\,0.3015\,$

$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.5\,$ $\,0.6915\,$ $\,0.6950\,$ $\,0.6985\,$
$\,0.6\,$ $\,0.7257\,$ $\,0.7291\,$ $\,0.7324\,$
$\,0.7\,$ $\,0.7580\,$ $\,0.7611\,$ $\,0.7642\,$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =15,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =2,$ and that the sample size $n=16.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(15,\frac{{2}^{2}}{16}) \\  & ∼N(15,0.25).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3) & =P(\frac{14.7-15}{\sqrt{0.25}}<Z<\frac{15.3-15}{\sqrt{0.25}}) \\  & =P(-0.6<Z<0.6) \\  & =Φ(0.6)-Φ(-0.6)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.6) & ≈0.7257 \\ Φ(-0.6) & ≈0.2743.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(14.7<\overset{―}{X}<15.3) & =Φ(0.6)-Φ(-0.6) \\  & ≈0.7257-0.2743 \\  & =0.4514.\end{aligned}
$$
